question: Why did the integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still show a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits?
expect: premise false: after system expansion the net climate-change impact was negative, −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t (a net benefit) (abstract)
rendered:
Environmental and Preliminary Economic Assessment of Integrated Resource Recovery from Spent Fluid Catalytic Cracking Catalysts

The integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still showed a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits because the credits depend on the selected avoided-product data sets, substitution ratios, and assumed functional equivalence. The net climate-change impact was −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t of spent FCC catalyst, indicating a net environmental benefit under the adopted product-substitution assumptions.
